intro.name: The beginning
intro.text: The healers and herbalists assemble around low tables laden with island plants, clean water, gourds, stone bowls, and carefully labeled samples. The judges announce several possible contests. Some reward a useful preparation; others are demonstrations of harmless magical craft. (Brewer) chooses an entry. A rival declares that (rival.his/her) mixture will be "the most powerful potion Isola has ever seen."

question.name: The choice
question.text: WHAT KIND OF POTION SHOULD (BREWER) MAKE?

choices.label: A POTION THAT DOES ONE SPECIFIC THING
THE MOST EFFECTIVE ANTIDOTE OR REMEDY

a1.text: The Careful Healer: Using established methods and careful observation, (Brewer) makes a useful preparation. The judges

a2.text: The Promising Discovery: The mixture appears helpful in controlled demonstrations, but the judges insist on further study before calling it a cure.

a3.text: The Beautiful Failure: The potion smells wonderful and looks magnificent but performs no better than plain water in the agreed tests.

a4.text: The Misidentified Leaf: A judge notices an ingredient mix-up before anyone uses the preparation. The entry is disqualified; the healer gains a lesson in careful identification.

b1.text: Strength of the Spirit: A fictional, magical preparation briefly grants an adult contestant unusual vigor. The effect fades harmlessly; (Brewer) wins a rare prize.

b2.text: The Boastful Brew: A rival proclaims extraordinary power, but a simple test reveals that the potion does nothing. The audience applauds the judge's deadpan expression.

b3.text: The Potion That Worked Too Well: A harmless fictional calming mixture leaves a judge sleepy through the awards ceremony. The organizers rule that "strongest" is not always "best."

b4.text: The Impossible Result: A glowing mixture behaves in a way no researcher can explain. It is sealed for further study;

c1.text: Exactly as Requested: The potion performs its assigned task reliably. (Brewer) wins.

c2.text: Almost Right: The color changes beautifully but to the wrong shade, or the fragrance fades too quickly.

c3.text: The Endless Bubbles: The mixture produces far more bubbles than intended. The judges struggle to keep straight faces.

c4.text: The Unexpected Utility: The mixture fails its assigned task but proves useful for marking baskets or decorating barkcloth.

lead_c.text: The judges randomly request a harmless effect: vivid color change, a pleasant fragrance, a long-lasting bubble, a safe cooling sensation, or an explicitly magical but temporary glow.

d1.text: The Thoughtful Researcher: (Brewer) correctly matches a known remedy to a simulated case.

d2.text: The Cautious Scholar: (Brewer) refuses to make unsupported claims. The judges commend the honesty

d3.text: The Great Mislabeling: Two harmless demonstration samples are swapped; an apprentice notices before judging. The organizers improve their labeling system.

d4.text: The Rival's Sabotage: A competitor tampers with the labels. An inquiry exposes the trick.

e1.text: A New Principle: A careful experiment reveals a useful property of an island plant.

e2.text: The Potion of Hiccups: A rare comic magical mishap gives an adult judge harmless hiccups until sunset.

e3.text: The Temporary Transformation: A rare magical potion briefly changes the brewer's hair color or makes (brewer.his/her) voice squeak. The effect wears off; the crowd is astonished.

e4_1.text: The Council Intervenes: The elders stop a reckless demonstration before anyone is harmed. (Brewer) may accept the correction and gain Research skill, or sulk and lose reputation.

coda_v22_6.text: The Shared Prize: A mixed-team victory helps ease a longstanding village-Isolan disagreement.
